confidence_notes: Food and drink prices come from three web searches of crowd-sourced cost-of-living sites: MyLifeElsewhere, a Numbeo page summary and an Expatistan cocktail page. These sites are not official and their figures do not always agree. The searches found a cappuccino at about INR 130-150 (about USD 1.5-1.6), a local beer at about INR 150-160 (about USD 1.7-1.8) and a basic meal at about INR 160 (about USD 1.7). The beer estimate was raised to allow for restaurant markup, and the basic meal was raised to fit a sit-down restaurant serving tourists. Numbeo's median mid-range meal for two is INR 750, but its reported range runs from INR 650 to 3,806. The estimate is placed above the median, near INR 1,500, because three-course meals in places tourists use cost more. The only direct cocktail figure is Expatistan's INR 326, which comes from 4 data points last updated in April 2024. The cocktail estimate is set somewhat higher, using the usual price ratio of cocktails to beer in India. No per-glass wine price was found. That estimate is based on Numbeo's mid-range bottle price of INR 550 (range INR 150-1,500) plus normal restaurant markup, where Indian wine is taxed heavily and costs more than beer. Varanasi is a religious city with limited alcohol service, and draft beer is rare there, so all alcohol anchors are low-confidence. INR was converted at about 88-90 per USD; this rate was assumed and not looked up. Accommodation figures are model estimates from general knowledge, not from searches or booking sites. They assume a July monsoon off-peak period with moderate demand. The FX observation is the RBA 4pm reference rate for 18 November 2026, as reported in a web-search summary of RBA pages. The rba.gov.au page itself was not opened to check the figure.
comparable_city_reasoning: This uses north Indian heritage and pilgrimage cities with heavy backpacker traffic, such as Rishikesh and Agra, as comparisons, and is scaled below Delhi price levels. Restaurant prices are adjusted upward from local crowd-sourced medians to reflect venues tourists use.
